steps.title: Know your models
steps.html:
Type each gray word in the Filter models box.

@MODELS@

This list is also on the Canvas tab in VR.

steps.title: Go on location
steps.html:
🔗 First time only: connect Canvas at xr.optimaed.com. See Having trouble in VR? below.

Open the On-Demand app. Click Explore. Type Playground in Filter environments. Click Playground, then Begin Solo.

steps.title: Build the scene
steps.html:
Press the top button on your right controller, then click Models. Hide the Frog and Snake where they blend in. Put the Monarch where birds can see it. Perch the Eagle up high. Set the Binoculars where you stand.

✋ Grab a model with the palm trigger. Use both palm triggers to make it bigger or smaller.
🗣 Say it out loud: “The ___ hides here because its ___ matches the ___.”

steps.title: Take the shot and send it
steps.html:
Stand back so the whole scene fits. Open your menu, click Library, then Camera. Click Take photo.

Click the Canvas tab and pick @CANVAS@. Click Choose from My Files, pick your photo, click Use this file, then Submit to Canvas. Look for the green Submitted tag.

🔁 Want to fix it? Move the models, take a new photo and send it again.

steps.title: Check and leave
steps.html: Press the Meta button, then click Quit. Check that your photo is in the Canvas assignment. Not there? Open Having trouble in VR?

studio.title: Build a critter

labels.start: Look at the habitat. Pick one of each.
labels.done: Three habitats, three animals, all adapted to their homes. Nice work, crew!

studio.look: Three real Florida homes. A habitat is the home where an animal lives. An adaptation is a body part or behavior that helps an animal survive there.
studio.do: Look at the habitat photo. Pick a color, a body part and a trick that would help an animal survive there. Then meet the real animal.

frames.lead: 1. Which critter did you like best?

studio.full: You built an animal for all 3 habitats and met the real ones. Your 2 sentences have at least 20 words.

trick.burrow: Digs a burrow to stay cool

habitats.name: White sand dunes
habitats.alt: White sand dunes with clumps of grass by the sea

ok.color: Yes! A pale animal is hard to see on white sand.
ok.part: Yes! Claws help dig into soft sand.
ok.trick: Yes! A burrow is cool and safe from owls.

miss.color: Look at the sand. Which color would an owl miss?
miss.part: The sand is soft and deep. What helps an animal dig?
miss.trick: The sun is hot and owls hunt here. Where could an animal hide?

habitats.done: You built a dune animal! Here is a real one.

real.name: Beach mouse
real.alt: A small pale beach mouse sitting on white sand
real.cap: A Perdido Key beach mouse. It is pale like the sand and digs burrows in the dunes. USFWS photo.

habitats.name: Green marsh
habitats.alt: A green marsh with tall grass and cattails by the water

ok.color: Yes! Green blends in with the grass and cattails.
ok.part: Yes! Sticky toe pads help it climb tall stems.
ok.trick: Yes! Sitting still keeps it hidden from birds.

miss.color: Look at the plants. Which color blends in?
miss.part: The plants are tall and thin. What helps an animal climb?
miss.trick: Moving gets you seen. What would help it hide?

habitats.done: You built a marsh animal! Here is a real one.

real.name: Green tree frog
real.alt: A bright green tree frog resting on a gray board
real.cap: A green tree frog. Its sticky toe pads hold on to stems, and its green skin blends in.

habitats.name: Forest floor
habitats.alt: Brown dead leaves and twigs covering the ground in a forest

ok.color: Yes! Brown and blotchy looks like old leaves.
ok.part: Yes! A hard shell keeps it safe.
ok.trick: Yes! It closes up tight inside its shell.

miss.color: Look at the leaves. Which color blends in?
miss.part: This animal moves slowly. What could protect its body?
miss.trick: It has a hard shell. How could it use it?

habitats.done: You built a forest floor animal! Here is a real one.

real.name: Box turtle
real.alt: A Florida box turtle with a dark shell and yellow lines
real.cap: A Florida box turtle near Flamingo, Florida. It can close its shell tight like a box.

voice.brief: Welcome to the rainforest, crew. We film Scene 30, Hide and Seek. Hide the animals where they blend in, then take the shot.
voice.step1: Before your headset goes on, meet your five models. Learn each gray search word. You will type it in VR.
voice.step2: Put on your headset. Click Explore, type Tropical, and pick Tropical Rainforest. Then click Begin Solo.
voice.step3: Hide the frog and the snake where they blend in. Show off the butterfly. Perch the eagle up high. Then tell me how they hide.
voice.extra: Got time? Add a plant where a little frog could hide. That shot is just for VR crews.
voice.step4: Step back so the whole scene fits. Click Library, then Camera, and take the shot. Then send it to Canvas.
voice.step5: Press the Meta button and click Quit. Then open Canvas. Your photo should be waiting there.
